use_cases.title: Text receptionist
use_cases.audience: Cleaners, tutors, repair shops and other local service operators.
use_cases.problem: Owners lose time collecting the same details and tracking unanswered inquiries while doing their main work.
use_cases.example: Gather job details by text, draft a reply, and ask the owner to approve a quote.
journey: The owner connects a dedicated line and configures service facts, intake questions, hours and escalation rules.
A customer texts an inquiry; approved intake questions collect the minimum details needed for a job summary.
The assistant answers approved FAQs and drafts a response; prices, bookings and commitments go to the owner.
The owner approves or edits the exact action, takes over the conversation, or schedules an allowed follow-up.
acceptance: A nontechnical owner completes inquiry, intake, approved response and follow-up from the dashboard.
No unapproved quote or booking is sent; edits invalidate approval of the previous action.
An opt-out or human takeover stops pending automation, and duplicate inbound events do not duplicate replies.
success_signals: Setup completion and time to first completed inquiry.
Owner interventions and time spent per resolved inquiry.

use_cases.title: Personal AI by SMS
use_cases.audience: Individuals who want to reach their chosen assistant through ordinary SMS.
use_cases.problem: Capturing a thought or delegating a small task should not require opening another app.
use_cases.example: Text your assistant a note or reminder; let approved routines communicate with selected contacts.
journey: The owner connects an assistant, pairs an owner channel, and chooses allowed contacts and routines in the authenticated dashboard.
The owner texts a note, question or reminder; the connector decrypts the selected conversation and uses the chosen AI.
The assistant answers the owner or proposes an action for another person; automatic sending stays within configured routines.
The owner reviews exceptions and can pause or revoke the connector.
acceptance: Notes, owner replies and reminders work without exposing bodies to relay logs or storage.
An incoming phone number alone cannot change permissions, disclose other conversations or approve sensitive actions.
Messages outside approved routines wait for authenticated approval; reminders expire instead of arriving after their useful time.
success_signals: Tasks completed by SMS without opening the dashboard.
Corrections, unexpected messages and repeat use by the owner.

use_cases.title: Agent task notifications and replies
use_cases.audience: Developers connecting an existing customer-controlled AI agent to their own SMS line.
use_cases.problem: An agent needs a scoped way to notify its owner, receive replies and request review without requiring the owner to keep an agent console open.
use_cases.example: Receive a task-completion text from your agent, reply with context, and review its proposed next action.
journey: The owner installs a supported client integration and completes a synthetic first exchange through guided setup.
For a later controlled-device pilot, the owner pairs a dedicated Android phone and SIM, compares fingerprints and grants selected read or send authority.
The existing agent requests a task-completion notification within the approved recipient, routine, timing and budget.
The authorized connector verifies and routes the owner reply; any commitment or changed scope waits for authenticated owner review.
The owner can take over, disconnect or revoke the agent and see whether work is queued, submitted, delivered or unknown.
acceptance: MCP, SDK and workflow actions share the same enforced permissions, suppression and honest delivery states.
Setup preserves existing client configuration and key ceremonies; agents never receive broad owner credentials or raw content keys in prompts.
Replayed events and ambiguous submission cannot create duplicate messages; untrusted SMS cannot grant permission.
The simulator sends no real SMS; carrier behavior requires a separate controlled-device verification.
The experience uses an owner-provided Android phone and SIM; number provisioning and emergency-delivery guarantees are outside its scope.
success_signals: Measured time and manual steps to the first synthetic exchange on supported clients.
Verified revocation, replay refusal, scope refusals and owner takeover in a controlled pilot.

use_cases.title: Repair and project updates
use_cases.audience: Repair shops, makers and small project-based businesses.
use_cases.problem: Customers need progress updates, and owners need a clear record of approval before additional work.
use_cases.example: Send a repair update and request approval before extra work.
journey: The owner records a job and selects update templates.
A job milestone triggers an approved status update to the customer.
Additional work creates an owner-approved request for the exact scope and amount.
A matching customer response is recorded; ambiguous replies or conflicting changes return to the owner.
acceptance: Approval is tied to the correct job and request version; a generic reply cannot approve unrelated work.
Replayed status events send no duplicate update, and changed work invalidates an earlier pending request.
Unanswered requests appear in the exceptions inbox; silence never counts as approval.
success_signals: Status inquiries avoided and time to customer response.
Additional-work requests resolved without manual follow-up.

use_cases.title: Cancellation-slot recovery
use_cases.audience: Appointment-based local businesses with a small opt-in waiting list.
use_cases.problem: A cancelled appointment leaves unused time while several customers may want the same slot.
use_cases.example: Offer an open slot in sequence and stop when one booking is confirmed.
journey: The owner enters an available slot and eligible waiting contacts.
The workflow offers it to one contact with an expiry before moving to the next.
An acceptance reserves the slot for owner confirmation; later responses cannot allocate it again.
Confirmation closes outstanding offers and cancels remaining reminders.
acceptance: Concurrent acceptances cannot allocate the same slot twice; expired offers cannot claim it.
No external calendar booking is implied: the first version uses owner-entered availability and owner confirmation.
The owner can cancel the offer, and an offline phone does not send expired invitations.
success_signals: Cancelled slots filled and time to confirmation.
Expired offers, conflicting replies and owner corrections.

use_cases.title: Wedding and event concierge
use_cases.audience: Couples, community organizers and hosts of small events.
use_cases.problem: Hosts need to reach guests personally and follow up without repeatedly messaging people who already answered.
use_cases.example: Send personalized invitations, collect RSVPs, and remind only unanswered guests.
journey: The host imports or enters a guest list with permission records, reviews duplicate contacts and previews invitations.
The host approves a paced batch with event details, recipient timing and expiry.
Replies update the correct guest record; ambiguous answers go to the host.
Reminders target unanswered guests only, and the host exports the final RSVP list.
acceptance: Each recipient receives an individual message without disclosure of other guest numbers.
Duplicate contacts, household replies and ambiguous names are reviewed before changing guest counts.
RSVPs and opt-outs cancel relevant unsent reminders; batch progress separates queued, submitted, delivered and unknown.
success_signals: RSVP completion and host follow-up effort.
Duplicate contacts resolved and unnecessary reminders prevented.

use_cases.title: Volunteer and shift coordination
use_cases.audience: Clubs, volunteer organizers and small teams.
use_cases.problem: Coordinators need to fill an opening without continuing to contact people after enough volunteers accept.
use_cases.example: Fill an open shift by text and stop requests once it is covered.
journey: The coordinator defines an opening, capacity, expiry and opt-in contact group.
An approved workflow sends paced requests and records replies.
The coordinator confirms volunteers within capacity; excess acceptances receive a reviewed response.
The workflow closes the opening and cancels remaining requests.
acceptance: Concurrent replies cannot exceed the opening capacity or assign one response to two shifts.
Expired or cancelled openings cannot be filled by late replies.
Participants can withdraw; reminders honor suppression and the latest assignment.
success_signals: Openings filled and coordinator messages per assignment.
Overbooking prevented and withdrawals handled.

use_cases.title: Household coordinator
use_cases.audience: Households coordinating routine errands and responsibilities.
use_cases.problem: Small recurring responsibilities are easy to forget or duplicate when coordination is scattered.
use_cases.example: Coordinate pickups, errands and recurring responsibilities through opt-in reminders and replies.
journey: An owner creates an opt-in household contact group and recurring reminders.
A member receives a task and replies to accept, decline or report completion.
The owner sees unanswered tasks and decides whether to reassign them.
Members can pause their reminders; completing a task cancels its pending follow-ups.
acceptance: One member cannot read another private conversation or change the owner settings by SMS.
Recurring reminders respect timezone changes, expiry, completion and withdrawal.
The workflow records acknowledgments without treating delivery receipts as task completion.
success_signals: Tasks acknowledged and completed.
Unwanted reminders and manual coordination effort.

use_cases.title: Community lending desk
use_cases.audience: Community groups sharing equipment or other reusable items.
use_cases.problem: Small lending programs need a simple way to accept requests and track availability and returns.
use_cases.example: Request equipment by text, confirm availability, and receive return reminders.
journey: The owner records items, availability and borrowing rules.
A member requests an item by text; the request enters the owner queue.
The owner approves a reservation and pickup details within available capacity.
Return reminders stop when the owner records the return.
acceptance: Concurrent requests cannot reserve the same item for overlapping periods.
Availability questions do not themselves create reservations.
Cancellation, opt-out and confirmed return remove the relevant scheduled messages.
success_signals: Completed loans and response time to requests.
Reservation conflicts and overdue follow-up effort.

use_cases.title: Operational acknowledgment
use_cases.audience: Small teams coordinating routine maintenance and service issues.
use_cases.problem: An alert is useful only when someone accepts responsibility and others can see that response.
use_cases.example: Notify a small team about a maintenance issue and record who will handle it.
journey: A configured integration creates a routine issue with an expiry and eligible contacts.
An approved workflow notifies the group and collects acknowledgments.
The owner confirms responsibility, or a configured single-assignee rule records the first valid acceptance.
Closing the issue cancels remaining reminders and records the outcome.
acceptance: Duplicate issue events do not create duplicate requests or assignments.
Delivery or silence is never recorded as acknowledgment; stale replies cannot reopen closed issues.
The workflow is described as routine coordination, with no emergency-delivery guarantee.
success_signals: Issues acknowledged and time to accepted responsibility.
Unanswered issues, duplicate alerts and assignment corrections.
